raw_case_text:
A 17-year-old primigravida from Latin America, who did not seek care during pregnancy reportedly due to her undocumented status and fear of consequences, presented to a local community hospital in labor. Duration of rupture of membranes (ROM) was unknown. Her RPR (Rapid Plasma Reagin) titer was reported as >1 : 64. Due to heavy meconium, the baby was delivered by emergency C-section. A female neonate weighing 2.81 kg was born at 37.3 weeks of gestation. The baby was hemodynamically stable and had Apgar scores of 9/9 at 1 and 5 minutes, respectively. However, the baby was noted to have persistent hypoglycemia despite regular feeds and was admitted to a level II NICU where blood work showed a RPR titer of >1 : 64, platelet count of 69 x 109/L, and cholestasis with direct hyperbilirubinemia. The patient was transferred to our hospital for level 3 NICU care and for further workup and treatment. Examination showed that the patient was jaundiced, lethargic, and tachypenic, and in mild respiratory distress (RR was 72/min). Physiologic reflexes and muscle tone were normal. There were no clinical features of congenital infection on examination.
Laboratory tests showed hypoglycemia (46 mg/dl), thrombocytopenia (69 x 109/L), and normal counts of leucocytes and neutrophils. Blood chemistry showed a total bilirubin of 11.4, with direct bilirubin of 7.00, indirect bilirubin of 4.4, and elevated liver enzymes (ALT/AST of 185/79 unit/L). CSF studies showed elevated leukocytes of 30/mm3, neutrophils of 46%, and elevated proteins of 106 mg/dl. No microorganism was found in CSF culture. CSF VDRL was 1 : 8 (reference range = <1.1), indicating the diagnosis of neurosyphilis. Testing for HIV, Rubella, CMV, and toxoplasma was negative. Blood HSV 1 and 2 PCR was negative. Nontreponemal serologic screen (RPR) was reactive with high titers of 1: 256. FTA-ABS was reactive.
The infant's long bone X-rays showed signs of syphilitic osteochondritis in all bones with zones of lucency seen bilaterally in proximal and distal ends of tibia and fibula, proximal humeral metaphysis, and proximal and distal femoral metaphysis suggestive of congenital syphilis infection. Abdominal ultrasound showed mild prominence of spleen for age with mild perihepatic free fluid. Chest radiograph showed absence of focal infiltrates, and no osseous changes were noted. Ultrasound of the brain revealed no specific pathology. Auditory examination using the optoacoustic emission test was normal. Ophthalmologic examination revealed no pathology. Intravenous penicillin G 50,000 u/kg/dose every 12 h for 7 days was started and switched to every 8 hours to complete a 10-day course. The clinical course remained stable throughout treatment. After starting the treatment, gradual improvement was noticed in platelet count. Hepatic cholestasis resolved and jaundiced improved.
The mother was also treated with three doses of long-acting Benzathine penicillin G (2.4 million units administered intramuscularly) at weekly intervals. The patient was discharged home with the mother after 18 days stay in the NICU. The infant was clinically stable and feeding actively. The following recommendations were given on discharge: monitoring by general pediatrician, follow-up with an infectious disease specialist, and repeat serologic testing at 3 months.
Ancillary support including social services was provided for education of available community and other resources and continued medical care at the time of discharge.

subjective.chief_complaint: A term female newborn (37.3 weeks' gestation) delivered to an unbooked 17-year-old mother presented in the immediate neonatal period with persistent hypoglycemia, cholestatic jaundice, lethargy, tachypnea, and severe thrombocytopenia.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Born at 37.3 weeks' gestation via emergency cesarean section for heavy meconium-stained amniotic fluid (birth weight 2.81 kg, Apgar scores 9 and 9), the newborn developed persistent hypoglycemia despite regular feeds, thrombocytopenia (69 x 10^9/L), cholestatic jaundice, lethargy, and tachypnea (respiratory rate 72 breaths/min), prompting transfer to a level III NICU.
subjective.past_medical_history: Born to an undocumented 17-year-old primigravida from Latin America who received no prenatal care during pregnancy and tested strongly RPR-reactive (>1:64) at delivery.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for neonatal lethargy, jaundice, tachypnea, and persistent hypoglycemia.

objective.physical_examination: Birth weight was 2.81 kg. On level III NICU admission, the neonate was icteric, lethargic, and tachypneic (respiratory rate 72 breaths/min) with mild respiratory distress, normal muscle tone and neonatal reflexes, and normal ophthalmic examination.
objective.routine_investigations: Neonatal blood tests showed hypoglycemia (46 mg/dL), thrombocytopenia (platelets 69 x 10^9/L), normal WBC and neutrophil counts, cholestatic hyperbilirubinemia (total bilirubin 11.4 mg/dL, direct bilirubin 7.00 mg/dL, indirect bilirubin 4.4 mg/dL), and elevated transaminases (ALT 185 U/L, AST 79 U/L). TORCH/infectious workup (HIV, rubella, CMV, Toxoplasma serologies, and blood HSV-1/2 PCR) was negative. Long-bone radiographs demonstrated diffuse bilateral symmetric syphilitic metaphyseal osteochondritis (radiolucent metaphyseal bands in the proximal/distal tibiae, fibulae, femora, and proximal humeri). Abdominal ultrasound showed mild splenomegaly and trace perihepatic fluid; chest X-ray, cranial ultrasound, and otoacoustic emissions (OAE) hearing screen were normal.
objective.advanced_workup: Lumbar puncture CSF analysis revealed pleocytosis (WBC 30/mm3, 46% neutrophils), elevated protein (106 mg/dL), negative bacterial culture, and a reactive CSF VDRL (titer 1:8).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Confirmed early congenital syphilis complicated by congenital neurosyphilis, polyostotic metaphyseal osteochondritis, cholestatic hepatitis, and thrombocytopenia, established via neonatal serum RPR titer of 1:256 (maternal RPR >1:64), reactive neonatal FTA-ABS, and reactive CSF VDRL (titer 1:8). Treated in the NICU with intravenous aqueous crystalline penicillin G 50,000 U/kg/dose every 12 hours for 7 days followed by every 8 hours for 3 days (total 10-day course), while the mother received 3 weekly intramuscular doses of benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units. Thrombocytopenia and cholestatic jaundice resolved, and the infant was discharged home in stable condition on day 18.
